text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1% today to $142.37, continuing a sharp two-week rally that's now up 13.76%. The immediate driver is escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Iran has intensified attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and targeted Saudi oil facilities, triggering concerns about global crude supply disruptions. Oil prices jumped on the news, with global crude now trading at $125 per barrel (up sharply from typical levels), and that higher price environment directly benefits ConocoPhillips as a major oil producer.

The broader context fueling this sustained rally is a genuine tightening in global energy markets: the International Energy Agency has warned of supply constraints, and diesel shortages are expected to persist into 2027 as Iran-related disruptions combine with falling inventories. For an oil and gas major like ConocoPhillips, this means higher realized prices for its production over a longer horizon, not just a one-day spike—which is why the stock has gained nearly 14% in two weeks rather than just bouncing on today's headlines.
